plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to bid a fraction (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $13, so I'll bid approximately $8.7 to maximize expected profit while maintaining a reasonable chance of winning against Betty and Charles.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against overpaying. My value is $15, so I'll bid 15 × 2/3 = $10 to maximize expected profit while still having a reasonable chance to win against competitors with lower values.

With uniform values on [0,49] and 3 bidders, the symmetric Bayesian-Nash equilibrium bid is (n-1)/n × value = (2/3) × value. My value is $47, so optimal bid ≈ $31.33. This balances winning probability against overpaying, maximizing expected profit given competitors likely bid similarly.
